title: SEA latency-first launch toolkit
content:
Purpose / one-line
This is a go-to-market toolkit for a "latency-first" commercial push in Southeast Asia (SEA): messaging, competitive notes, sales enablement, sample announcements and an operational checklist focused on local regions, edge routing and low-latency SLAs. Draft for review by GTM + Solutions Eng.

Audience & priority segments
- Primary: Product/Platform engineering teams at scale-ups and marketplaces in SEA (e‑commerce, real‑time comms, gaming) that are latency-sensitive and cost-conscious.
- Secondary: Mid-market enterprises in finance/insurtech requiring private deployments with audit controls.
- Tertiary: Local cloud integrators and ISVs (resellers, channel partners).

Core value props to emphasize (short hooks)
- Predictable low-latency inference across hosted + dedicated + private deployments in SEA regions.
- Unified runtime: ship identical API & rollout behavior whether on-hosted or in-customer VPCs (reduces dev velocity risk).
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations tuned for common SEA workloads (chat, recommendation, rerank).
- Reliability with graceful fallbacks: cross-region routing + model variant fallbacks keep live UX steady when local capacity spikes.

Positioning statements (options for copy)
- Lead headline: "Ship real‑time AI in SEA — fast, reliable, and predictable."
- Supporting: "Redwood Inference gives you consistent, low‑latency LLM serving across hosted, dedicated and private environments — with regional routing and cost controls that scale."
- Elevator pitch for Sales decks (30s): "For product teams building latency sensitive AI features in SEA, Redwood provides a production-grade inference runtime and ops layer that guarantees predictable latency, reduces per‑token cost, and keeps your deployment options open across hosted, reserved and private environments — all with the same API and observability."

Differentiation vs common buyer alternatives
- Build self-hosted: faster time-to-value vs building your own runtime + observability, lower ops burden. Emphasize customer stories where in-house attempts hit unpredictable tails and cost overruns.
- Global cloud managed endpoints (big cloud vendors): better regional latency and inference economics for specialized LLM workloads; highlight model/kernel selection and batching optimizations specific to LLMs.
- Other LLM API vendors: we provide deployment parity (hosted ⇄ private) and explicit tooling for cost/latency tradeoffs (Optimize recommendations).

Competitive landscape (notes for quick call prep)
- Major cloud managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI): strong enterprise trust and integrations; typical weakness: higher tail latency for small sequence workloads, less model-specific kernel optimization; also limited rollout patterns for private/on‑prem parity.
- LLM API players (OpenAI, Anthropic): strong high-quality models + dev ergonomics, but regional availability and VPC/private parity often limited; pricing unpredictable for high throughput.
- Inference infra vendors (Replicate, Runpod, Lambda Labs, Cortex): offer hosting/self-serve; differentiators include price and openness. Risk: they lack Redwood’s end-to-end rollout, cost tooling, and enterprise observability.
- Local competitors / system integrators: some regional companies offer managed GPU clusters — good for pure capacity but weaker on LLM-specific scheduling, KV caching, and unified API.

Top objections & suggested rebuttals
- "We already use cloud vendor X": Acknowledge trust, then highlight where Redwood reduces per-token cost and improves p99 latency for interactive flows due to kernel selection, batching and caching. Offer a latency benchmark kit we can run together.
- "Why not self-host?": Point to hidden costs (SRE time, kernel tuning, tail latency debugging). Offer a TCO estimation playbook and a short pilot with predictable SLAs.
- "Data residency / compliance": Reassure with Private deployment + VPC options, KMS integrations, and audit log examples; escalate to security team for contract-level guarantees.

Enablement assets (what to produce before launch)
- One‑pager: "Latency first for SEA" (sales leave-behind).
- Technical benchmark kit: simple repo + instructions to benchmark local p50/p95/p99 vs cloud baseline (runbook for Solutions Eng).
- 4 slide battlecard: competitors + rebuttals + pricing math.
- Email + Slack announcement copy for customers and partners.
- 2 technical playbooks: "Hosted → Dedicated migration" and "Private deployment checklist (VPC+KMS)" for SE-Asia infra partners.
- Recorded demo: 8–10 min demo of a real-time chat + rerank pipeline showing p50/p95 numbers (scripted).

Sample timeline (high level)
- Week 0: finalize messaging + approve SLA language.
- Week 1: enable solutions engineering + finish benchmark kit.
- Week 2: sales training + partner webinar.
- Week 3: soft announcement to pilot customers / early partners.
- Week 4: public launch + blog + region-specific assets.

Pricing framing & early commercial motions
- Launch offer idea: 3 months of discounted Dedicated capacity + free benchmarking/architectural review for first 8 SEA customers (apply).
- Pricing talk track: show per‑token vs cloud baseline and include dedicated capacity commit options for predictable throughput.
- Channel motion: identify 3 APAC cloud integrators to pilot resell + implementation packages.

Operational checklist for launch (quick bullets)
- Confirm region readiness: local infra + edge routing rules in prod.
- Validate latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for test workloads.
- Set up trial capability and apply promo codes for pilot customers.
- Prepare SRE on‑call coverage for first 30 days post-launch.
- Legal: run standard data residency clause + partner contract templates.

Customer-facing sample announcements (copy drafts)
- Short email subject: "New: Low‑latency LLM inference in SEA — now available"
- Email body (short): "We’re excited to announce Redwood Inference’s low‑latency inference available in Southeast Asia. Ship real‑time AI with predictable latency and cost controls across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. If you build chat, recommendation or real‑time features, we’d love to run a short benchmark with your team. Reply to this email to get started."

Internal Slack announcement (short)
- "Heads up — SEA latency-first launch next week. Priority for marketplaces/gaming/fintech accounts. Sales playbook + benchmark kit in the GTM folder. Reach out to @Tomás for partner intros."

Open questions / follow-ups (TODO)
- Confirm list of initial pilot customers (A: outreach underway — Simran).
- Which local cloud partners are cleared (legal/contract) for resell in SG, ID, PH? (Eunji will confirm).
- Need final SLA wording sign-off from Legal on SLA credit playbooks for p99 misses.
- Should we bake a specific low-latency model family recommendation (quantization) per workload? Ask Applied ML to provide 2 model+quant profiles.

Appendix: quick benchmarking checklist for SE teams (for Solutions Eng use)
- Test workload definitions: chat (prompt 40–60 tokens, reply 80–150), rerank (50 items), embedding (batch 128).
- Measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens baseline.
- Run cross-region fallback test (local region saturated -> fallback to nearest warm region) and measure added latency and error rate.
- Document and store benchmark results in the shared spreadsheet (link to be added).

Notes to self (rough)
- Keep messaging simple: "predictable latency" resonates more than "SLOs" in early customer outreach.
- Use local case examples where possible (e.g., a SEA gaming studio reduced chat latency from 220ms to 85ms after optimization — anonymize if needed).
- Avoid deep technical parlance in top-line customer copy; put technical detail in battlecards and playbooks.

---
End of draft. Please add any missing customer contacts, partner approvals, or legal comments in the Confluence ticket: confluence:RWI-SEA-EDGE-1.
